title: Chrome Rim Drift
description: One metallic sample shredded into a clicky garage rim/clave layer: striate interleaves the grains while a perlin pan LFO scatters them across the stereo field, drifting on its own clock. Over 23 cycles the striate count, playback speed, bit-crush grit and shape drive all morph on prime periods so the metallic cloud never settles, with a tight delay-only tail and no reverb.
code:
setcpm(132/4)
stack(
  s("metal*4")
    .striate("<8 12 6 16 8 24 6 12>/8")
    .speed("<1 1 1.5 1 -1 1 0.5 2>/8")
    .n("<0 2 1 3>/4")
    .pan(perlin.slow(13).range(0.08, 0.92))
    .pan("<0.5 0.2 0.8 0.35 0.65>/16")
    .hpf(sine.slow(23).range(380, 1400))
    .bpf(saw.slow(11).range(900, 5200)).resonance(sine.slow(7).range(6, 15))
    .crush("<16 12 8 10 14 6>/16")
    .coarse("<1 1 2 1 4 1>/11")
    .shape(sine.slow(29).range(0.18, 0.52))
    .gain(perlin.slow(17).range(0.55, 1.0))
    .struct("x x ~ x x ~ x*2 x".euclid(7, 8))
    .degradeBy(sine.slow(16).range(0, 0.35))
    .sometimesBy(0.18, x => x.speed(-1).striate(4))
    .off(0.0625, x => x.gain(0.3).hpf(1600).pan(0.85).crush(6).striate(16))
    .delay("0.32:0.09375:0.55").delayfeedback(sine.slow(19).range(0.2, 0.55))
    .gain(0.95)
)
